body.x: AeiROBOT Co., Ltd. (CEO Sheal Eum) participated in the “HUMANOID M.AX Alliance” pavilion at CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), where it showcased the “ALICE” series.

AeiROBOT is a startup that develops humanoid robots capable of replacing all types of labor that humans can perform, under the vision of “A Robot for All.” True to the meaning embedded in its name, the company aims to realize a humanoid platform that moves alongside people and creates practical value.

Founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the research team of Professor Jaekweon Han of the Department of Robotics Engineering at Hanyang University ERICA (HERoEHS), AeiROBOT began its path toward commercialization by leveraging robotic technologies developed in the laboratory. In its early stage, the company demonstrated its technical capabilities by participating in the development of the AI-based autonomous soccer humanoid robot “ALICE,” which achieved results in the RoboCup Humanoid League. It later introduced various robot platforms, including the welcome robot “Aimy” and the companion robot “Edie,” and it now accelerates its entry into the global market as its technology and growth potential gain recognition.

AeiROBOT emphasized that it now receives recognition as a specialized “physical AI” robot company capable of commercialization, beyond the level of simple research robots. The company’s core technologies are broadly into hardware and software.

On the hardware side, the company highlights its in-house-developed linear actuator technology, which serves as the muscles in robots. This actuator moves away from conventional rotation-motor and reducer-based systems, enabling more precise force-based control and a more natural physical interaction. The company explained that this technology serves as a key factor that simultaneously improves humanoid robot performance and reduces manufacturing costs.

On the software side, AeiROBOT internalizes AI-based autonomous system technologies, including the use of “Isaac GR00T,” a full-body control AI platform for humanoid robots. This technology integrates walking control, environmental perception, and autonomous decision-making, allowing robots to collaborate with humans and create value in real industrial sites and everyday spaces.

body.cap: Visitors watch a demonstration of the humanoid robot “ALICE” at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AeiROBOT recently completed a Series A investment round worth approximately 10 billion won. In addition, the company was selected as a partner in NVIDIA’s Inception Program, which supports promising startups. Through this partnership, AeiROBOT secured a technological foothold to adopt and optimize NVIDIA’s next-generation humanoid robot foundation model, “Isaac GR00T,” at an early stage. Furthermore, through collaborations with several major global tech companies, the company leaves open the possibility of joint research to embed large action models (LAMs) into robot hardware, preparing to leap beyond being a hardware manufacturer into a global AI platform company.

As external proof of its technological capabilities, AeiROBOT points to its consistent achievements in the RoboCup Humanoid League. Working with a research team led by CTO Jaekweon Han, the company achieved strong results on the global stage with the autonomous soccer humanoid robot “ALICE,” proving that its control technology, which enables robots to make decisions and walk autonomously in complex environments, has reached world-class levels. These technological assets now carry over into “ALICE 4,” the fourth-generation humanoid, which evolves into high-performance hardware that reduces noise while enabling precise force control.

Based on these achievements, AeiROBOT now concretizes proofs of concept with major domestic conglomerates and industrial sites. Focusing on industries facing severe labor shortages, such as manufacturing, logistics, and construction, the company aims to complete validation by 2028 and then deploy robots on real sites to generate tangible revenue, turning its commercialization roadmap into reality.

As a member of the “K-Humanoid Alliance,” AeiROBOT presented its booth in pavilion form at CES 2026. Through the “ALICE” series, the company demonstrated how robots can solve real challenges in industrial environments.

body.cap: ALICE M1 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: AeiROBOT’s ALICE M1 and ALICE 4 optimize their hardware for “mobility” and “general-purpose labor,” respectively, reflecting actual industrial site requirements.

ALICE M1 is a mobile manipulator that combines a wheeled base with a humanoid upper body. AeiROBOT cited the model’s superior mobility and work efficiency as its greatest strengths. It enables faster, more stable movement than bipedal robots while performing precise logistics picking and assisting with assembly using its two arms. The company emphasized that the robot moves agilely even in narrow factory aisles, making it a practical solution optimized for logistics centers and manufacturing lines that require immediate deployment.

ALICE 4, which concentrates AeiROBOT’s technological capabilities, is a next-generation bipedal humanoid that mimics the human body structure. According to company representatives, by mounting in-house-developed linear actuators on all joints, the robot simultaneously achieves rough-terrain walking and precise force control, which conventional robots struggle to achieve. ALICE 4 moves freely in unstructured environments with stairs or obstacles and performs tasks using the same tools as humans. This means companies can deploy robots directly into existing industrial sites without modifying facility structures.
These two lineups share an AI platform based on Isaac GR00T and offer an optimal portfolio for users to select based on site difficulty and purpose.

At this exhibition, AeiROBOT demonstrated ALICE robots performing high-complexity tasks while safely collaborating with humans in complex, unstructured environments such as manufacturing, logistics, and construction, by combining linear-actuator-based precise force control with physical AI. Through this, the company conveyed that humanoids no longer represent future technology but rather tools that create immediate value in real-world settings.

body.cap: Components of the humanoid robot “ALICE.” | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Regarding this, an AeiROBOT official said, “This CES participation serves as an opportunity to show that Korea’s humanoid robot technology has reached a global level, while presenting a vision to partners worldwide as a ‘general-purpose robot platform ready for immediate field deployment.’” The official added, “Starting with CES 2026, AeiROBOT aims to expand global PoC partnerships and realize the vision of ‘A Robot for All’ across industrial sites worldwide, standing tall as a game changer in the global humanoid market.”

In this way, AeiROBOT plans aggressive business expansion to rise as a mainstream player in the global humanoid market. The company aims to successfully complete demonstration projects at manufacturing, shipbuilding, and construction sites by 2028 and then begin mass production of affordable humanoids. It also expressed ambitions to solidify its business model as “robots that actually generate revenue.”

For overseas markets, the company sets major European manufacturing powerhouses as its primary targets. It plans to supply ALICE 4 and ALICE M1 to countries such as Germany, the United Kingdom, France, and Italy, which once centered on the automotive industry but now face labor shortages and structural industrial changes, positioning itself as a partner that helps restore industrial competitiveness. To this end, AeiROBOT plans to proactively pursue global certification processes in response to the EU AI Act and the new Machinery Regulation.

In the long term, the company also presented a vision to expand its business beyond hardware sales into a Robot as a Service (RaaS) model that combines an AI platform serving as the robot’s brain with maintenance services.

body.x: The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
